content:
emma_oncall: taking over night shift — opening handoff thread. Incident currently open: INC-2026-99. symptoms: regen-service /v2/generate returning 500s and partial outputs for ~6-9% of requests. first pager at ~23:12 UTC. affected regions: eu-west, us-west. likely correlated with model-variant rollout 2026-04-14T22:45 (regen-v2-quant). primary: emma_oncall, secondary: lee_sre for first 2h, then handback to eu-night team.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-99 · Severity: P1 · Pager triggered by alert: prod.regen.500-rate > 5pct for 5m · Incident page: <https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-99>

lee_sre: quick summary of what I've done so far:
- rolled traffic for a subset of tenants to regen-v1 fallback.
- started canary rollback for regen-v2 on us-west (50% traffic rollback in progress).
- enabled short-circuit cache for common prompts to reduce load.

logs snippet (from regen-worker-5):
```
2026-04-15T22:58:03Z ERROR regen.handler request_id=abc1234 handler=generate timeout processing kv-cache miss -> downstream ModelRuntimeError: kernel-launch-failure
stack: ModelRuntimeError at inference/kernel.cu:422
```

commands I used / useful checks:
```
# pod status in affected ns
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=regen-service -o wide
# tail logs for a single pod
kubectl -n inference logs regen-worker-5 -c regen --since=10m | grep "ModelRuntimeError" -n
# traffic routing check
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/internal/routing?route=/v2/generate | jq .revisions
```

opsbot: DEPLOY BOT: Rollback PR #3421 (regen-v2 -> regen-v1 canary) started by lee_sre. status: in-progress. CI checks passed.

miguel_support: customer impact notes so far:
- LumenAI: 12 support tickets since 22:50 UTC complaining about 500s in their regression tests. Ticket REF-1882 opened, customer asked for ETA.
- ParcelBot: intermittent failures on long-context prompts; they reported timeouts and some degraded outputs.
- ~0.8% of free-trial sessions observed a hard 500. Most paying customers see partial mitigation by fallback.
Suggested customer message (draft):
"We're aware of an issue causing occasional 500 errors for text generation. We've routed some traffic to a known-good model and are rolling back a recent variant. We expect reduced errors in the next 15-30 minutes and will follow up when fully resolved."

sarah_prod: ops checklist / runbook pointers:
- Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/regen-service-incident (see section: canary rollback & per-tenant fallback).
- If rollback doesn't reduce 500s within 15m, trigger full rollback and open emergency capacity (reserved pool) to absorb requests.
- Watch these dashboards: Dashboards > Regen Service > Errors, Model Runtime KPIs, KV Cache Evictions.
- Escalation path: if customer-impacted tenants > 3 OR global 500-rate > 5% for 10m -> page SRE lead + oncall-manager.

emma_oncall: current active mitigations (stateful):
- Partial canary rollback: us-west 50% -> oks in progress (opsbot reports in channel).
- Tenant-level fallback mapping applied for LumenAI and ParcelBot.
- Short-term rate-limit on long-context requests (context > 2048 tokens) = 10rps per-tenant.
- KV-cache TTL increased from 60s -> 300s for hot prefixes.

what I need from lee: 1) confirm whether kernel failure is hardware (GPU driver) or model compile issue; 2) any hot pods with OOMs / retries?

lee_sre: quick answers:
- no OOMs observed in last 30m; errors tie to kernel-launch failures in cuda driver stack on regen-worker-5 and regen-worker-7. both are on instance type g5-large-02.
- I've flagged the two nodes with node taints and re-scheduled pods to fresh nodes as a mitigation. node replacement ongoing.
- model compile paths look OK locally; suspect driver flakiness after recent kernel module update last week. coordinating with infra to check node driver versions.

commands to continue watching:
```
# check node kernel/driver versions
kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, kernelVersion:.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion, gpuDriver:.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion}'
# list pod restarts
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=regen-service -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
```

opsbot: NODE ACTION: cordon node g5-node-178 && drain --ignore-daemonsets (initiated).

miguel_support: pulling together customer comms: I'll notify LumenAI support lead with the drafted statement, link to status page, and a rough ETA 30m. will CC account exec. ParcelBot has a dedicated slack they prefer — pinging them now.

emma_oncall: operational checklist I'm leaving for night team taking over at 00:30 UTC:
- primary: emma_oncall until 00:30, then hand to eu-night (oncall: ana_eu). secondary remains lee_sre for first 2 hours.
- watch metrics: prod.regen.500-rate (alert if > 5% sustained 10m), prod.regen.latency-p95 (> 3s), model.kv_evictions rate spike.
- current mitigations to maintain: canary rollback progress, tenant fallback mapping (do NOT remove), short-circuit cache TTL increased.
- runbook link again: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/regen-service-incident -> follow 'rollback -> node replacement -> escalate' section.
- pager rules: if incident-bot marks P1 -> escalate to oncall-manager and send bridge link to #incident-bridge.

sarah_prod: small note on cost/QA: full rollback will increase latencies for some requests but reduces error rate. prioritize customer impact over micro-latency for now.

emma_oncall: leaving a live checklist as I sign off briefly (will stay reachable on pager):
- confirm opsbot shows rollback completion (PR #3421 merged + deploy completed).
- confirm LumenAI sees <1% 500s for 15m before we mark reduced impact.
- if kernel failures persist after node replacement, escalate to infra-driver team (pager: infra-driver).

lee_sre: acked. I'll keep an eye on node taints/drains and follow infra-driver if we see re-occurrence. planning to reimage g5-node-178 if driver mismatch confirmed.

miguel_support: cc: support triage docs updated with messaging. I'll post customer update once rollback confirmed.

incident-bot: UPDATE: INC-2026-99 status changed -> Mitigating. Active mitigations: canary rollback, tenant fallbacks, node drains.

emma_oncall: handoff note complete. last_message_ts: 6479991450. signing off for a short break, will re-check in 8m. if anyone picks up earlier, pls @emma_oncall. :thumbsup:
